about: Every friction a reader meets on this site, structured: who, where, what they tried, what happened, what they expected, the evidence, who can fix it and whether it landed. Kept by sherpa@php.newsroom; see admin/sherpa/README.md. Synthetic readers are test instruments, not people: their findings are prompts, and each is re-checked on the current version before it is logged.

frictions.reader: board member, phone
frictions.intended: Learn in seconds, between meetings, whether to worry
frictions.actual: Four blocks of site machinery come before the briefing: the masthead with Ask and Feedback, the 'New to this story?' banner, the 'Your reading' tracker with five buttons, and the RESEARCH band. The headline starts 649px down an 844px screen; the thirty-second answer is below the fold.
frictions.expected: The headline and the thirty-second answer on the first screen
evidence: synthetic board run 2026-10-22T1753Z on v0.4.3 (top fail, high)
synthetic designer run 2026-10-22T1753Z on v0.4.3 (top fail, high)
sherpa walk on v0.8.1: h1 top at 649px on briefings/board/, 631px on briefings/cto/ and briefings/pm/, 569px on claims/, 550px on the front page (390x844, mobile)
telemetry to v0.5.9: 107 of 275 events (39%) from phones
UF-001 point 5: a real reader finds pages dense with icons and links (see F011)
UF-002 point 6
UF-003 point 3: a fourth reader
synthetic board and designer, run 2 on v0.10.18: still two screens of controls before the briefing on a phone; the designer counts three boxes now
11:45 pass on v0.14.17: the headline starts 603 to 671px down on a phone on every page walked (source, articles, fact-check, explore, gaps, join)

frictions.proposal: On phones, collapse 'Your reading' and the origin band into one line under the standfirst (or behind a 'Reading tools' toggle), and show the 'New to this story?' banner only on the front page and only once. Target: h1 inside the top 250px of the first screen.

frictions.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
frictions.actual: Reproduced, and it is unreachable by design: the card is drawn with pointer-events: none, it closes as soon as the pointer leaves the word, and 'Open the glossary' is plain text, not a link. The card promises an action it cannot give. Clicking the word itself does open the glossary, but nothing says so. On a touch screen the card cannot be opened at all without following the link.
frictions.expected: Quick and honest: change the line to 'Click the word for the glossary entry'. Proper: make the line a real link to the term's glossary entry, let the card take the pointer (pointer-events: auto) and keep it open for a short grace period while the pointer moves from the word to the card; on touch, the first tap opens the card and the link inside it goes on. Keyboard: focus already opens it; Escape closes it.
evidence: UF-001 point 10, received 2026-10-23
